text:
HMRC has recovered just over £8m from crypto investors through its disclosure facility.

502 settlements across two tax years (According to the FT)
The FT ran the numbers this week.

Here is what they actually tell you, and what they don't.

The split:
2024/25: 280 settlements, £3.5m
2025/26: 222 settlements, £4.8m
Average settlement around £16,600.

Data via an FOI request from compliance firm Identomat.

Notice the shape of that.
Fewer people settling. More money collected.

HMRC isn't casting a wider net. It's landing bigger fish. The cases coming through now are more substantial than the early ones.

Now the reality check nobody will put in a headline.

The FCA reckons around 7 million UK adults hold crypto.

502 settlements. £8m.

That is a rounding error. HMRC is not collecting at scale yet.

£8m is not the story. The story is what got built to collect it.

Around 65,000 crypto nudge letters went out in the year to April 2025.

More than double the year before.
Over 100,000 in four years.

Those letters are the funnel. Settlements are what comes out the other end, eventually.

And from January 2026, CARF.
Exchanges reporting user data to tax authorities automatically, across borders.

The old model was HMRC asking exchanges for data. The new model is exchanges handing it over without being asked.

So the £8m figure is a lagging indicator of a system that was still being assembled.

The next few years of numbers will look very different, because the data arrives whether HMRC goes looking or not.

One thing I'm seeing on live cases that the coverage misses:

HMRC officers are increasingly challenging the output of crypto tax software rather than accepting it.

A Koinly report is a starting point, not a defence. If the cost base is reconstructed badly, they will find it.

Practical position if you have undeclared crypto gains:

Coming forward unprompted gets you materially better penalty treatment than being found.

That gap is the whole game. It closes the moment a letter lands on your doormat.

And if you've already had a nudge letter and ignored it, you're now in the worst category. Prompted, and arguably deliberate.

The window for the cheap version of this closes quietly.

If you're sitting on years of unreported crypto and don't know where to start, that's what we do all day.

text:
Yesterday we explored Proof of Work (PoW) and how Bitcoin secures its network.
But not every blockchain uses mining.

So how do modern blockchains like Ethereum validate transactions?

Let's find out.

WEB3 WITH MUHOX — Episode 08 

What is Proof of Stake (PoS)?
When Ethereum launched, it used Proof of Work, just like Bitcoin.
But in 2022, Ethereum made one of the biggest upgrades in blockchain history.
It switched to Proof of Stake (PoS).
Why?

Let's understand.
What is Proof of Stake?
Proof of Stake (PoS) is a consensus mechanism where people lock up (stake) their cryptocurrency to help secure the blockchain.
Instead of miners competing with powerful computers
Validators are selected based on the amount they have staked and the network's rules.
Why Was Proof of Stake Created?
PoS was introduced to solve some of the challenges of Proof of Work:
Reduce energy consumption.
Improve scalability.
Lower the cost of securing the network.
Allow more people to participate without specialised mining equipment.

How Does Proof of Stake Work?
Imagine a community wants someone trustworthy to keep records.
Instead of holding a competitio
Members deposit a security bond.
The network randomly selects one validator from those who have staked.
If that validator behaves honestly:
✅ They earn rewards.
If they try to cheat:
❌ Part or all of their stake can be taken away (this is called slashing on some PoS networks).
Real-Life Example
Think of a trusted referee in a tournament.
Before officiating, the referee deposits a guarantee.
As long as they remain fair, they keep the guarantee and receive payment.
If they cheat, they lose their deposit.
That's similar to how PoS encourages honest behaviour.

Advantages of Proof of Stake
✅ Much lower energy usage.
✅ Faster transaction processing on many networks.
✅ No expensive mining hardware required.
✅ Easier for more people to participate.

Challenges of Proof of Stake
⚠️ Large holders may have greater influence.
⚠️ Different PoS blockchains use different validator selection rules.
⚠️ Security depends on good protocol design and decentralisation.

Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake
Proof of Work
Proof of Stake
Uses miners
Uses validators
Requires computing power
Requires staking coins
Higher energy consumption
Lower energy consumption
Bitcoin
Ethereum, Cardano, Solana and many others
Common Misconception
Many people think:
PoS is simply "holding coins."
Not true.
Staking involves participating in securing the network according to that blockchain's protocol. Simply owning coins in a wallet is not always the same as actively validating.

Key Takeaway
Proof of Work secures a blockchain through computational work.
Proof of Stake secures a blockchain through economic commitment.
Both aim to achieve the same goal:
A secure and trustworthy network.

Would you choose:
⚒️ Proof of Work
or

Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake
If you have spent time in crypto
You have probably heard these two terms:
Proof of Work (PoW)
Proof of Stake (PoS)
But what do they actually mean?
Let's break them down.

What is Proof of Work (PoW)?
Proof of Work is the consensus mechanism introduced by Bitcoin.
Instead of trusting one person
Thousands of computers compete to solve complex mathematical puzzles.
The first computer to solve the puzzle earns the right to add the next block.
This process is called Mining.

Why is it called "Work"?
Because computers must perform real computational work.
They consume electricity and processing power to secure the network.

That's why it's called Proof of Work.
Advantages of PoW
✅ Extremely secure.
✅ Battle-tested for over a decade.
✅ Very difficult to attack.
Disadvantages of PoW
❌ High energy consumption.
❌ Slower transaction speed.
❌ Expensive mining equipment.

What is Proof of Stake (PoS)?
Proof of Stake takes a different approach.
Instead of competing with powerful computers...
Participants lock up (stake) their coins.
The network then selects validators to create and verify new blocks.
The more you stake, the greater your chance of being selected—but every blockchain has its own rules.

Advantages of PoS
✅ Uses far less energy.
✅ Faster transactions.
✅ Lower operating costs.
✅ Easier to scale.

Disadvantages of PoS
❌ Requires users to stake assets.
❌ Different networks use different validator selection models.

Neither is universally "better."
It depends on the goals of the blockchain.
If maximum security is the priority...
PoW has a strong track record.
If speed, efficiency, and lower energy use matter more...
Many modern blockchains choose PoS.

Both Proof of Work and Proof of Stake exist for one purpose:
To keep the blockchain secure and ensure everyone agrees on valid transactions.

La acusación sostiene que empresas vinculadas al régimen obligaban a buques comerciales a contratar un supuesto "seguro marítimo" para transitar por la vía estratégica, cobrando incluso en Bitcoin y otros activos digitales para evadir sanciones.

La medida también amplía el cerco contra la llamada "flota en la sombra" iraní: ocho buques petroleros y varias compañías navieras fueron sancionados por transportar millones de barriles de crudo y productos petroquímicos hacia China y otros destinos. Desde enero, OFAC ya ha sancionado más de 100 embarcaciones relacionadas con esta red.

El mensaje de Washington es claro: impedir que Teherán utilice el comercio marítimo internacional para sostener sus ingresos petroleros y financiar operaciones del IRGC.
